deep.reconstruction:
This page contains no mathematics. It is part of a German-language set of notes, apparently lecture or study notes, headed 'Geschichte von Sparta' on the previous page (folio 58). It is a continuous prose summary of ancient Spartan history.

Content of folio 59, in order:
(1) Before Lycurgus the Spartan constitution was badly disordered and inequality of wealth grew very large. This opened the way to unrest, which lasted until Lycurgus' age, c. 880 BC.
(2) Lycurgus is introduced as coming from one of the two ruling houses and as guardian of the young king Charilaus.
(3) The state commissioned Lycurgus to reform it. Sparta was small and surrounded by other states. His legislation therefore aimed to give it enough strength to dominate its neighbours. He made the nation into warriors and kept as much of the old constitution as possible.
(4) The kings remained but were limited by a Senate (gerousia). An interlinear and marginal insertion mark (x / double-dagger) points to an addition, probably the popular assembly.
(5) The warriors were also to farm, so the land was redistributed: 9000 lots for the Spartans and 30000 for the Lacedaemonians (perioikoi). These lots could not be sold.
(6) No precious metals and no coined money were allowed.
(7) Citizens were to regard themselves as a brotherhood, so 12 to 20 always had to eat together (syssitia).
(8) Unhealthy persons were restricted (probably in marrying), and only healthy children were to be raised.

The numbers on the page are historical figures, not computations: the dates c. 880 and c. 1080 (the latter on the previous page), and the counts 9000, 30000 and 12-20. There is therefore nothing to reconstruct mathematically.

The handwriting is a looser, more rounded German Kurrent than Gauss's usual hand. The marginal fragments on the left belong to the facing page. The leaf may be a student's or family member's history notes that ended up bound in the Nachlass bundle, rather than Gauss's own work. This is my assessment and is uncertain.
errors: No mathematical errors, since there is no mathematics on the page.

Historical content is consistent with the traditional ancient accounts (Plutarch, Life of Lycurgus): 9000 lots for Spartiates and 30000 for perioikoi, Lycurgus as guardian of Charilaus, gerousia, ban on gold and silver coinage, syssitia, exposure of weak infants.
The date c. 880 for Lycurgus follows the traditional chronology (Eratosthenes / Apollodorus, c. 884 BC). Modern scholarship considers Lycurgus semi-legendary.
Plutarch gives about 15 per mess; the page's '12-20' is a reasonable paraphrase.

results.what: Summary of the Lycurgan reforms of Sparta (land division into 9000 Spartiate and 30000 perioikic lots, gerousia, ban on coinage, syssitia, eugenic child-rearing)
results.usually_credited_to: Ancient sources, chiefly Plutarch's Life of Lycurgus; standard school and university history curricula c. 1800

deep.surprise_reason: The page is routine historical study notes on Sparta with no mathematical content. Its standard textbook material (possibly not even in Gauss's hand) carries no significance for the history of mathematics.

checkable.asserts: Total number of land lots in the described redistribution (trivial arithmetic; the only numerical content).

transcription_corrections: Line 4: 'Hervor[?] und eine der herrschenden Familien' is unclear. Sense: Lycurgus came 'aus einer der herrschenden Familien'. The opening word is probably part of '... trat hervor' or 'Er war aus'.

Line 11: the machine reading '[-ve-]erhielte[?], formte[?] seine Nation' is better read as a struck fragment followed by '(be)hielte, formte seine Nation zu Kriegern'. Read with line 10, the sense is that he wished to gain and keep superiority over the neighbours.
Line 13: the struck text is 'behielt, er'. A caret/x mark after 'Könige' and a double-dagger after 'beschränkt' refer to insertions, probably in the margin or lower on the page.

Line 20: the line beginning 'Edle Metalle' carries an x/double-dagger insertion mark at its start, linking it to the earlier mark. 'herrschen[?]' at the end of line 21 is uncertain; the sense is 'circulate / be used'.

Last two lines: 'Ungesunde Personen durften sie[?] [?] halten[?]' more plausibly reads 'Ungesunde Personen durften sich nicht verheirathen', followed by 'und nur gesunde Kinder durften auferzogen werden'. A double-dagger footnote mark sits under 'durften'.
'Lacedaemonier' is underlined in the manuscript, as are 'Lycurgs' (line 3) and 'Charilaus' (line 5).
